messages:
mira: Heads-up: after the kernel-selector tweak that prefers fused-attn for llama2/3 we saw a 12-18% P99 latency regression on Llama-13B workloads. investigation shows repeated KV cache evictions during chat-like prompts (many short turns).

sahil: Can you paste the top of the profile? is it kv eviction code path or memcpy?

mira: Quick profile (5m sampling, tail-heavy):
```
Top ops by CPU ms:
 - compute_attention_kernel_fused       4200ms
 - kv_cache_evict_path                  3100ms  <-- spikes correlated with tail
 - kv_cache_write                       900ms
 - aten::reshape                        520ms
 - fused_silu_forward                   480ms
```
Notable: eviction spikes line up with inputs that have chat template prefixes (~400-800 tokens) + short responses.

jonathan: Hmm. two hypotheses: (1) rope_theta default drifted between Llama2 vs Llama3 model configs, so prefix hashing / cache key calculation differs and we end up missing cache entries more often, causing re-populate and eviction churn; (2) kernel-selector prefers fused-attn which increases per-request working set (KV memory layout change) and pushes us past the eviction threshold sooner.

kevin: I also noticed the batcher currently uses raw token count to decide flush thresholds. For KV-heavy models we should add a kv_size heuristic: head_dim * num_heads * dtype_bytes * seq_len. If kv_size > X then lower batch size. Proposed config snippet: 
```
batching.heuristics:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  kv_eviction_threshold: 0.65    # fraction of KV pool usage to trigger eviction
  kv_size_weighting: true
  prefer_streaming_kv: false
```
This avoids building too-large contiguous KV objects for fused kernels.

perf-bot: ALERT: upstream latency SLO violation detected for model redwood/llama-13b at 1768504337. P99 increased from 220ms -> 265ms. Related metric: kv_evictions/sec +42%.

mira: Confirmed. The weird part: same workload on older runtime (pre-selector-change) had identical throughput even with rope differences. So selector + kv-policy interaction seems likely.

sahil: Quick test idea: pin rope_theta to 10000 and force legacy attention kernel (non-fused) for a canary. If latency drops -> selector is root cause. Can you create a canary config?

mira: Created canary tag kv-heuristic-v2 that pins rope_theta and forces kernel=legacy for llama variants. small config we pushed to canary: 
```
model_overrides:
  redwood/llama-13b:
    rope_theta: 10000
    runtime:
      kernel_selector: prefer_legacy
```
Deployed to 1% traffic.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: kv-heuristic-v2 -> 1% (canary-id: ckv-2026-05-14-01) :rocket:

kevin: If that helps, we should change the selector rule to consider kv_pool_pressure before preferring fused kernels. Fused is great for pure compute but bad when it increases live KV footprint during interaction workloads.

jonathan: Also double-check RMSNorm vs SiLU fused kernels — for Llama3 we saw a small regression when silu-fuse path was taken with small batches (extra kernel launch overhead). Might be compounding.

mira: Agreed. Next steps: (1) run the canary and collect P95/P99 and kv eviction rate (2) add kv_size-aware batching heuristic to staging config and bench (3) audit rope_theta defaults across model catalog to ensure consistent cache keys for chat templates.

sahil: I'll run a synthetic load (chat simulated distribution: prefix 512-1024 tokens, reply 8-64 tokens) and post numbers. Command I use: 
```
./perf_runner --model redwood/llama-13b --canary-tag kv-heuristic-v2 --clients 50 --seq-dist chat --profile --out perf_kvcanary.json
```
Expect results in ~30m.

perf-bot: Note: adding kv_size to batching heuristic may change cost/throughput tradeoffs. please add a metric for tokens/s GPU and token-cost delta to the rollout checklist.

mira: Will do. If the canary looks good we'll roll to 20% and also try just the batching change (without forcing legacy kernel) to see if that resolves without sacrificing fused-kernel peak perf.

jonathan: One more thing — chat templates that append system messages at runtime are causing variable prefix lengths; consider normalizing to a capped prefix window when computing and storing KV keys. That would drastically reduce eviction churn for very long system prompts.

kevin: Good call. I'll draft a PR with kv-aware batcher + prefix-capping. Will include a feature-flag to A/B toggle.

mira: Thanks all. I'll paste canary numbers when perf_runner finishes. :thumbsup:
